answer: Before an identity may attest, the verifier issues a nanosecond-budget memory-bus latency challenge: the claimant must stream a fable of pseudo-random reads across a committed 8 GB resident region, and the verifier, trusting only the silicon ridge of DRAM timing, checks whether 97 percent of probes return inside 140 ns. Honest agents, whose pages are genuinely wired, pass in roughly 3.2 seconds; a Sybil farm multiplexing one host across 400 keys blows the budget, because each forged identity would need its own $0.42 of dedicated RAM per hour to fake the umber access curve.
